articles.title: 'It's a miracle' - fireball crash victim Millroy praises rescuer Hartog
articles.summary: British racing driver Ollie Millroy says it is a "miracle I'm alive" after fellow driver Loek Hartog "did everything right" when saving him from his blazing car.
body: Millroy, 36, was hit by two other cars during the China GT Championship race at the Shanghai International Circuit 11 days ago, with his Ferrari immediately catching fire before hitting the safety barriers.
A barely conscious Millroy was stuck in his car for over a minute before he was pulled from the burning wreckage by Dutchman Hartog after he immediately stopped his car to help him.
"He acted instantly and he did everything right," a recovering Millroy told BBC Sport from his hospital bed in China.
"Watching the video back, it looks like you're watching a movie and everything's rehearsed.

articles.title: USA exits U-20 World Cup on penalties as tournament’s timing draws criticism
articles.summary: Brazil advances to quarter-finals in Poland. Americans have not won tournament since 2012. US youth teams have struggled in recent showings. The United States were eliminated from the U-20 Women’s World Cup in the last 16 on Wednesday, falling to Brazil on penalties after playing to a 1-1 draw…
body: The result extends a difficult run of form for US youth national teams across the men’s and women’s programs. This is the third time since last October that a US youth team has failed to win a knockout game at a World Cup: the U-17 boys and the U-17 girls both exited in the last 16 of their respective tournaments in shootouts. The U-20 men fell in the quarter-final of their World Cup in October 2025.

The US, holders of 2024 Olympic gold in women’s soccer and winners of two of the past three senior Women’s World Cups, last won the U-20 tournament in 2012, with a squad headlined by Crystal Dunn, Julie (Johnston) Ertz and Sam Mewis, all of whom are now retired.

In Poland, the Americans struggled to advance from their group, losing the opener against Italy before playing Japan to a 2-2 draw. A 9-0 rout of New Zealand was enough to reach the knockout round as one of the tournament’s top third-place sides. Brazil comfortably finished atop their group, beating Tanzania, Canada and England by a 9-2 aggregate.

articles.title: ‘They are very similar’: Arsenal’s Dowman reminds Merino of Lamine Yamal
articles.summary: Teenager continues development with two goals at Ipswich. Merino: ‘He is a big talent and we have to take care of him’ Mikel Merino says Max Dowman reminds him of Lamine Yamal after the Arsenal prodigy continued his development by scoring twice in his side’s 4-2 win against Ipswich.
body: Dowman, who has been given a host of opportunities at senior level by Mikel Arteta, starred after being handed his first appearance of the season, at Portman Road on Tuesday. The 16-year-old attacker’s classy double eased Arsenal into the last 16 of the Carabao Cup and left Arteta admitting that containing the hype around the England youth international is not an easy task.

Arsenal are managing Dowman carefully and Merino is well placed to see how young talents can benefit from listening to managers and older players. The Arsenal midfielder plays with Lamine Yamal for Spain and believes Dowman is as fearless as the 19-year-old winger.

“There are some similarities in terms of their character,” he said. “They don’t care about the spotlight. They thrive when pressure is at the highest. They are always up for the challenge and they are not shy at all – even facing the biggest names in the game.”

Merino, who also scored against Ipswich, raved about Dowman. “He is an unbelievable talent. We knew it, but every time he goes on the pitch and plays against grown men he makes the difference. He is a big talent and we have to take care of him.

articles.title: Saudi club given stadium ban over Jota chants towards Neves
articles.summary: Saudi Pro League side Al-Taawoun are ordered to play two matches behind closed doors after supporters taunted Ruben Neves over the death of friend Diogo Jota.
body: Saudi Pro League side Al-Taawoun have been ordered to play two home league matches behind closed doors after their supporters taunted Al-Hilal midfielder Ruben Neves over the death of his friend and team-mate Diogo Jota.
Liverpool forward Jota died in a car crash at the age of 28 in July last year and was a close friend of midfielder Neves, having played alongside him for Wolverhampton Wanderers and Portugal.
Neves also now wears the number 21 shirt for Portugal in Jota's memory, and has a tattoo on his calf of him and Jota embracing. He was also a pallbearer at Jota's funeral.
Supporters targeted Neves before his side's 6-0 win on Saturday by repeatedly shouting "Jota" at him.

articles.title: African greats inspired by the potential of Nairobi 2029
articles.summary: Some of Africa's great track and field stars expect the decision to award Kenya the 2029 World Athletics Championships to inspire the next generation.
body: The decision to award the 2029 World Athletics Championships to Nairobi has prompted an outpouring of celebration across Africa.
Ethiopian great Haile Gebrselassie, a two-time Olympic 10,000m champion, congratulated the whole continent on the "wonderful news" following the announcement by World Athletics on Tuesday morning.
The Kenyan capital saw off former Olympic Games hosts London and Rome to secure a slice of history, with the event set to be held in Africa for the first time.

Unsurprisingly, news that the globe's top athletes will descend on the 48,000-capacity Kasarani Stadium in three years' time has gone down well with some of East Africa's biggest track and field stars.

The comfortable victory was important for an Atletico side with lots of new faces still bedding in, after two defeats in their three matches prior.
Ademola Lookman fired over and Lee was denied by Osasuna stopper Aitor Fernandez as Atletico started well. At the other end Rojiblancos goalkeeper Jan Oblak made a fine save to deny Raul Garcia.

David fired Atletico ahead midway through the first half with a quick reaction to finish off a rebound after his first shot was saved following enterprising work by Alejandro Grimaldo on the right wing.

articles.title: Djokovic to return to China Open on Sky Sports after 11-year absence
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic has confirmed he will compete at the China Open this year, which runs from September 30-October 6 live on Sky Sports, marking a return to the event following an 11-year absence.
body: The 39-year-old recently dropped as low as No 12 in the world rankings following a shock first-round defeat to Argentina's Mariano Navone at the US Open.

That defeat followed on from a third-round exit in May at the French Open - two underwhelming Grand Slam displays coming either side of a run to the semi-finals at Wimbledon, where he was well beaten in straight sets by eventual champion Jannik Sinner.
Djokovic has not won a Grand Slam title since 2023, going three full calendar years without success.
Returning to the ‌ATP 500 event in Beijing, Djokovic is a six-time winner having last competed there in 2015. Sinner won the title last year, but is currently out with a knee injury.

articles.title: Arsenal icon breaks silence after accepting a new job
articles.summary: Patrick Vieira has broken his silence after agreeing to become the new manager of Senegal, becoming the latest high-profile coach to enter international management. In recent years, several coaches have moved from club management to the international game, with Jurgen Klopp and Carlo Ancelotti…
body: International management was not always viewed as an attractive option for coaches at the club level, and taking charge of a national team was sometimes seen as a role that managers pursued later in their careers.

However, the arrival of coaches such as Klopp and Ancelotti in international management has added greater prominence to the role. England are also coached by an elite manager in Thomas Tuchel, further highlighting the level of coaches now working with national teams.

Vieira has had spells at clubs including Crystal Palace, Nice and Genoa, and he will now take charge of Senegal, one of the top countries in Africa. Expectations will therefore be high as he begins his new role with the national team.

The former Arsenal midfielder will bring his experience from club management to an international environment, where he will have the opportunity to work with Senegal’s players and prepare the team for their upcoming challenges.

articles.title: F1 announce 2027 calendar and increase in Sprint rounds
articles.summary: Formula 1 has announced its 2027 calendar and an increase in the number of Sprint weekends from six to 10, with the season starting in Bahrain.
body: For a fourth consecutive year, there are 24 rounds scheduled with Portugal's Portimao and Turkey's Istanbul Park returning to the calendar.

As expected, the Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort falls off the schedule while the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya moves into a rotational deal with Spa-Francorchamps that will see the Spanish event held in even numbered years from 2028 and the Belgian Grand Prix held in odd numbered years from 2027.

F1 had delayed its calendar announcement for next year due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, which has created uncertainty over the end of the current season with Qatar and Abu Dhabi still currently scheduled to take place later this year.
Bahrain will host a four-day pre-season test on February 24-27 before holding the 2027 season-opener on March 12-14 and it will be a Sprint weekend, with the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix a week later.

articles.title: Arsenal? Chelsea? Man City? Which club has most valuable teens?
articles.summary: The Premier League's teenage sensations are making headlines after Max Dowman's starring display for Arsenal and JJ Gabriel's revelation that he wants to leave Manchester United.
body: Dowman, 16, scored twice in Arsenal's Carabao Cup win over Ipswich, only hours after 15-year-old Gabriel had stunned Manchester United with his request to cancel his registration at the club.
Dowman's breakthrough and Gabriel's desire for first-team opportunities show how the stars of tomorrow are starting younger, but which Premier League clubs have the most valuable teens?

For this week's Between the Lines, we use Transfermarkt valuations to rank Premier League clubs by teenage value, albeit with the caveat that Transfermarkt does not assign valuations to young players with no first-team experience such as Gabriel.
According to Transfermarkt, Manchester City have the most valuable teenagers at a combined £122.6m, putting them just ahead of Chelsea on £121m, and Arsenal in third on £102.4m.
